question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{60}^{∘})=\frac{1}{2}$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$ what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x-{60}^{∘} & ={30}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & x-{60}^{∘} & ={150}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our two equations for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={30}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={150}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ x & ={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={210}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={90}^{∘}$ and $x={210}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ So, the solutions are $x={90}^{∘},{210}^{∘}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=90\cdot 210=18\,900.
$$
